resolutions.researcher_notes: Status inferred from context (no literal 'operating' token required per SOP). CEM/UN case study: Uthmaniyah Gas Plant 'commissioned in 1981 as part of Saudi Aramco's Master Gas System' and describes it as one of Aramco's largest operating gas plants. MEED: 'The Master Gas System is operated by Saudi Aramco' and 'developed to transport gas across the kingdom' with Uthmaniyah among the network's active processing plants. Both establish the Uthmaniyah gas transmission infrastructure is in operation. Segment-specific ('UA-1-km199') naming is not present in any public source, so support is class/context-level, not segment-level; rated medium. The gem.wiki page's own cite (OPEC ASB 2012 p.75) is a dead link and is a country-level statistics bulletin that never supported this segment.

Fuel=Gas is unambiguous. CEM case study: Uthmaniyah Gas Plant 'processes natural gas' (Khuff/associated gas). MEED: Master Gas System 'developed to transport gas across the kingdom.' Two independent sources both identify this as gas infrastructure feeding/serving the Uthmaniyah gas plant.

LengthKnown=108 km is not stated by any locatable public source. The value derives from the Petroleum Economist / SDE World Map geometry dataset (the 'UA-1-km199' ID is a dataset segment label, not a named line). gem.wiki cites OPEC ASB 2017 p.92, but that URL is dead (redirects to an HTML shell) and OPEC ASB is a country-level statistical bulletin that does not enumerate individual pipeline lengths. No independent corroboration for 108 km found; leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating support.

Diameter='24, 32' in is not stated by any locatable public source; it derives from the PE/SDE geometry dataset. gem.wiki cites OPEC ASB 2017 p.92 for this, but that URL is dead and OPEC ASB does not list per-pipeline diameters. No independent source names a 24/32-inch line to Uthmaniya. UNRESOLVED (no fabrication).

Endpoint Uthmaniya / Eastern Province / Saudi Arabia directly corroborated. CEM case study: 'Uthmaniyah Gas Plant (UGP), located ~177 km southwest from the company headquarters at Dhahran city in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia.' MEED: Uthmaniyah named among the Master Gas System processing plants in the kingdom. Two independent sources place the Uthmaniya gas plant (the pipeline's stated end point) in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. StartLocation is blank in the record and not sourced.

Owner=Saudi Aramco (100%) corroborated. CEM case study repeatedly attributes the Uthmaniyah Gas Plant to 'Saudi Aramco' (owner/operator). MEED: 'The Master Gas System is operated by Saudi Aramco.' Two independent sources agree the Uthmaniya gas transmission infrastructure is a Saudi Aramco asset; no competing owner found.
